articles.title: RESEARCH FINDS TOP-PERFORMING MARKETERS DID THESE THINGS DIFFERENTLY IN 2026

articles.title: HOLIDAY ADS ARE STARTING EARLIER. SHOPPERS MAY NOT BE.
articles.summary: Retailers are increasing holiday ad spending earlier in the year, but consumers are not necessarily starting their shopping earlier. Nielsen found six times more holiday advertising in September than five years ago, while historical data shows that holiday ads on connected TV can generate up to 3.2 times the sales lift of non-holiday ads. The earlier push gives brands more time to build awareness and consideration, but it also risks ad fatigue before shoppers are ready to buy. An earlier advertising schedule does not mean an earlier customer journey, so brands need to build interest before introducing timely offers that give consumers a reason to purchase.

articles.title: WHY SOME SHOPPERS SKIP COUPONS—EVEN WHEN THEY OFFER A DEAL
articles.summary: Consumers who believe businesses use discounts for self-serving reasons are less likely to redeem coupons. Research found that shoppers with higher power distance beliefs often question whether a coupon represents genuine savings or signals inflated prices or product problems. You can improve coupon redemption by clearly explaining the offer, addressing skepticism about pricing, and offering price-matching guarantees. The research also found that coupon campaigns may perform better in regions with lower power distance beliefs, making cultural attitudes a useful factor in audience targeting.

articles.title: SPEND 80% ON SEO AND 20% ON AI SEARCH
articles.summary: SEO budgets shouldn't shift to AI search based on visibility metrics alone. One founder's data showed Google organic search generated 146 qualified leads in 6 months compared to just 5 from AI search. The recommended approach is to allocate roughly 80% of resources to SEO fundamentals and 20% to AI search experiments. Track results and prioritize the AI platforms your actual buyers use.

articles.title: JUST ADMIT “I DON'T KNOW”
articles.summary: Admitting when you don't know an answer can increase customer trust and purchase intent more than giving a vague response. A study found that vague answers made customers up to 16% less likely to buy than answers that acknowledged uncertainty and promised to find the information. This effect was strongest when customers suspected salespeople had a personal financial incentive, such as earning commission. Explain how you'll get the answer rather than leaving customers with uncertainty, since a clear and honest response makes you seem more trustworthy and collaborative.

articles.title: THE TEAMS BUILDING AI MAKE THEIR SLIDES WITH PITCH
articles.summary: Pitch is how AI leaders like Perplexity, Legora, and Synthesia create on-brand decks at scale. With Pitch, you can collaborate on fully editable presentations and unlock agentic workflows, like personalizing slides with CRM data and call notes.

articles.title: YOU CAN NOW ADD AMAZON AFFILIATE LINKS TO YOUR INSTAGRAM REELS
articles.summary: Instagram is expanding its shopping features by letting eligible US creators add Amazon affiliate links directly to Reels and feed posts. Creators earn commissions on qualifying purchases without Instagram taking a cut. Product links also work in carousels and support affiliate platforms like LTK and ShopMy. Creators can now turn entire product collections and gift guides into shoppable content using a single link.

articles.title: HOW GOOGLE REDIRECT URLS CAN DISTORT A RANK-TRACKING EXPORT
articles.summary: Google rank-tracking tools can record a result's position without identifying the actual page it links to when Google redirect URLs are not properly identified. In one November 2026 snapshot, 63 of 65 organic results contained these redirects, making URL comparisons unreliable because different redirect links can lead to the same page. Check where each link leads before analyzing keyword overlap, page rankings, or site visibility. Keep the original URLs, provider, and collection date so your SEO reporting remains accurate and easy to verify.

articles.title: HOW (& HOW NOT) TO USE AI FOR KEYWORD RESEARCH
articles.summary: AI is most useful for keyword research when it analyzes data a business already has rather than generating keyword lists from scratch. Customer emails and call notes can be turned into search phrases, with the customer's original wording kept separate from AI suggestions. A short brief listing services, location, and what the business doesn't offer stops the model from suggesting irrelevant keywords. Search Console exports and PPC search terms reports can then be sorted into page assignments and negative keyword candidates, with every figure checked in the source platform.

articles.title: SAME QUESTION, 1,000 TIMES
articles.summary: A test comparing 1,000 ChatGPT responses found that model updates can dramatically change which businesses get recommended, even when nothing about the businesses changes. One model favored a single directory in 82% of answers, while the newer model cross-checked multiple sources, including licensing records and business websites. The findings raise questions about the reliability of one-time visibility checks.

articles.title: HOW I BROKE THROUGH MY AI PLATEAU
articles.summary: After hitting an AI plateau, the author found new momentum by building a personal app to surface overlooked photography and creating a shared “marketing brain” in GitHub with Claude. The experience reinforced the value of solving personal problems with AI and exchanging practical learnings with peers. Rather than treating AI as a fixed set of workflows, the approach is to keep experimenting while protecting skills, like writing and critical thinking, that are worth developing independently.

articles.title: WHAT WE LEARNED BY WATCHING CLAUDE READ ZAPIER.COM
articles.summary: Zapier built an experimental tool to test how Claude interprets website content. When testing its Slack integration page, the team discovered that Claude wasn't reading the modified webpage directly. Instead, it retrieved a Markdown version and passed the content through another AI model before the main model processed it. This means changes to a webpage's HTML may not affect what AI agents actually see. Testing how AI reads Markdown content is just as important.
